correctness.rationale: For each lattice band the central probability is obtained by exact geometric-tail summation. The threshold equation has the explicit solution \(q_s=\exp[-2\operatorname{arsinh}(c/(\sqrt2 s))]\). Writing the complementary band infimum as \(\exp[-(2s-1)t_s]/\cosh t_s\) gives a derivative strictly below \(-2t_s+2\tanh t_s<0\), so the first band is globally extremal. Endpoint inclusion is handled separately, proving nonattainment for the closed event and unique attainment for the open event. No finite computation is used to establish an infinite claim.

value.rationale: The source explicitly treats one standard deviation as a distinguished concentration scale and computes only that point for the symmetric geometric family. The new theorem replaces that isolated value by the exact standardized concentration profile for every positive radius, distinguishes open from closed endpoint behavior, and proves the structural fact that the first lattice contact is always globally extremal. This is a natural complete classification of the scale parameter, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
